clue.text: Demand and get something repealed?

definitions.meaning: to demand payment or obedience is to insist on it
read cryptically, a law that has been repealed becomes an ..., a former statute

explanation.surface: A campaigner both insists on something and wants a law scrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: split as EX ACT it describes an act of parliament that is no more.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is a verb meaning to insist on or extract payment or compliance.

clue.text: Historic cutter last seen sinking in lake

definitions.text: Historic cutter last seen sinking in lake

parts.words: Historic cutter last seen sinking in lake
parts.note: a legendary sword, the cutter, was thrown back to the Lady of the Lake as King Arthur lay dying

explanation.surface: A famous old boat was last spotted going down in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' suggests a sailing vessel, but here it is a blade: Arthur's sword was returned to the lake at the end of the legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthurian legend has the king's magic sword caught by a hand rising from a lake and drawn under.

clue.text: Suggest more rides, heading off to take in hard US mountains

indicators.note: the outer letters take in, or enclose, the word for hard

parts.note: to suggest more of something is to propose that it be added
iron is proverbially hard, as in iron will

indicators.note: the word for rides loses its first letter, its heading

parts.note: a hack is a ride on horseback, so rides are hacks

explanation.surface: Someone proposes extra rides before heading off to a tough American mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: A hack is a leisurely ride on horseback; 'heading off' removes its first letter, and 'to take in' sets the word for hard inside the rest after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adirondacks are a mountain range in upstate New York.

clue.text: Time without resources upset soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: someone without resources is poor

explanation.surface: Penniless and fed up after a long stint, the soldiers are disgruntled.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns the word for without resources upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a body of soldiers, and troops is a common word for soldiers generally.

clue.text: Description of organic chemicals misapplied to lab mice

indicators.note: things misapplied are put in the wrong places, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A laboratory note on organic compounds wrongly used on test mice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misapplied' rearranges the nine letters of TO LAB MICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Metabolic is an adjective for the chemical processes and compounds of living things, so it describes organic chemistry.

clue.text: Low blast of siren indicates astronomical event

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: a blast scatters things, so the letters of the following word are blown into a new order

explanation.surface: A deep wail from a siren announces something happening in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective describing the blast but is the cow's verb; 'blast of' rearranges SIREN into NRISE.
explanation.definitionFit: The appearance of the moon above the horizon is an event studied in astronomy.

clue.text: Disastrous instant almost blocked by newspaper

indicators.note: the shortened word is blocked by, or filled with, the word for newspaper
the word for instant is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a tick is an instant, as in 'just a tick'
rag is a dismissive term for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A disaster struck in an instant, almost stopped by the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instant' tempts you towards trice, but the shortened word must leave room for the newspaper after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic and disastrous are synonyms describing events causing great suffering.

clue.text: Viking chief unhappy to organise the horde, initially

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling unhappy

indicators.note: the opening letters of the three words before it are taken

explanation.surface: A gloomy Norse leader sets about marshalling his warriors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes O, T and H from organise, the, horde. Harald Bluetooth was a tenth-century king of Denmark and Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: Harald Bluetooth was a Viking king, giving his name to the wireless technology.

clue.text: Went down after dropping second group

indicators.note: the word is taken after it has dropped a letter

parts.note: a team that went down was beaten, so it lost

explanation.surface: A team was relegated after losing their deputy, and then a whole group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after dropping' takes S out of LOST.
explanation.definitionFit: A lot is a group or set of items, as at an auction or in 'this lot'.

clue.text: Country's borders initially closed to the French transport

indicators.note: the borders of the word are its first and last letters
only the first letter of the following word is used

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A nation's frontiers were at first shut to French vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' takes C and Y from COUNTRY; 'initially' takes C from closed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicycle, or cycle, is a common means of transport.

clue.text: Who benefits? Youngster bagging one on heading over

indicators.note: the word for youngster bags, or holds, the numeral

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a young scout
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A child pockets a coin and asks who stands to gain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bagging' puts I inside CUB; 'heading' takes O from over.
explanation.definitionFit: Cui bono is a Latin phrase asking who stands to gain, used when looking for a motive.

clue.text: A question applied to a movement of water

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary movement of a muscle

explanation.surface: A query arises about how water moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'applied to' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquatic is the adjective for things living in or relating to water.

clue.text: Plastic building material not good for sign

indicators.note: not here means without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: Lego is the plastic toy brick used for building models

explanation.surface: A plastic used in construction isn't fit for making a signboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic building material' sounds like industrial supplies, but it is the toy brick.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo, the lion, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Reworked scene with priest's resolution

indicators.note: something reworked is made over again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter, so the word priest is used as written in the mix

explanation.surface: A rewritten scene features a cleric's firm decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reworked' rearranges SCENE and PRIEST together; the possessive adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolution in the sense of steadfast determination is close in meaning to persistence.

clue.text: Source of patriotism making half of no sense? Not at first

indicators.note: one of the two letters of the short word is taken, its first half
the word for sense is used without its first letter

parts.note: rationality is good sense, reason

explanation.surface: Patriotism, it seems, makes little sense, though not at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes N from no; 'Not at first' drops R from RATIONALITY, leaving ATIONALITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to a nation, one's citizenship, is what patriotic feeling springs from.

clue.text: University residence recalled amongst most successful in city

indicators.note: the pieces sit amongst, inside, the word for most successful

parts.note: the best is the most successful

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pad is slang for a home or residence

explanation.surface: A university hall, remembered among the city's finest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns the slang word for a home backwards; 'amongst' sets it, with the university letter, inside the word for most successful after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital city of Hungary.

clue.text: Father's written about love between woman and men and other events

indicators.note: the word for father is written around the other pieces

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: the letter for love goes between the two words for people

parts.note: hen is informal, chiefly Scottish, for a woman
taken as written
love means nil in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: Dad has written about love affairs between women and men, among other things.
explanation.walkthrough: Hen is a Scottish informal word for a woman; 'between' places the love letter between the two words for people, and 'written about' wraps the father round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are occurrences or observable happenings, so they are events.

clue.text: Courage — traditional presentation of beer?

definitions.meaning: in British slang, ... is nerve or courage
beer has long been sold in glass containers

explanation.surface: Courage is also a British brewery, so the clue reads as a brewer's classic way of selling its beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Courage is a British beer brand, which makes the two definitions look like one.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses bottle for nerve, and beer is served in glass vessels.

clue.text: Basic line in Early English not making sense?

indicators.note: the letter for line goes in the abbreviation for Early English

parts.note: mental, informally, means crazy, not making sense

explanation.surface: A fundamental line in Old English text appears nonsensical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside EE to give ELE.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental means fundamental or essential, relating to first principles.

clue.text: Perhaps gossip columnist's money's good woman's introduction to corruption

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is a gossip writer as an example of a busybody

parts.note: a quid is a pound, British slang for money
a nun is a good, pious woman

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tabloid columnist's earnings are a decent woman's first step into corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that a gossip columnist is one example of the answer, a busybody.
explanation.definitionFit: A quidnunc is an inquisitive gossip, someone eager for news, as a gossip columnist is.

clue.text: Move fast to see salad plant

definitions.meaning: to shoot up or zoom, as prices or a car might
a peppery leaf, also called arugula

explanation.surface: Hurry along to look at a lettuce.
explanation.definitionFit: To rocket is to zoom, and rocket is a peppery salad leaf, called arugula in America.

clue.text: Move even faster to see US monument

definitions.meaning: to hurry still more, rush plus more
the South Dakota mountain carved with four presidents' faces

explanation.surface: Speed up even more to visit an American landmark, following on from the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition splits as RUSH MORE; the clue echoes the one before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Rushmore in South Dakota is carved with the faces of four US presidents.

clue.text: Two points cropping up in actual murders

indicators.note: in a down clue, cropping up means rising, so the letters read upwards
the letters are found in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A couple of key details arise in real-life killings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds TUALMU in acTUAL MUrders; 'cropping up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An umlaut is the pair of dots placed over a vowel, as in German.

clue.text: Acted about second toilet being 'inconvenienced'

indicators.note: the word for acted goes about, around, the other pieces

parts.note: to act is to do, so acted is did
a commode is a chair with a chamber pot, a toilet

explanation.surface: Someone performed around a second lavatory, which was a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the pieces inside the word for acted, before its last letter. The quotes hint at the toilet joke in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Discommoded is a formal word for troubled or put out.

clue.text: Drink? Mug with a bit of Darjeeling brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means raised, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: mug is slang for a face

indicators.note: only one letter, the first, of the tea's name is used

explanation.surface: A beverage: a mug with a little Darjeeling tea served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a cup but means a face; 'brought up' turns FACED round.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaf is decaffeinated coffee or tea, a drink.

clue.text: Cleaner, abandoning most of toilet is put off

indicators.note: the word for cleaner abandons, loses, some letters

parts.note: detergent is a cleaning agent

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the gents is the British name for a men's public toilet

explanation.surface: A cleaning product leaving most of the lavatory dirty is a turn-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' cuts GENTS to GENT; 'abandoning' removes GENT from DETERGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter someone is to discourage them from acting.

clue.text: Fear getting in the way when reversing

indicators.note: the found letters are then read backwards
the letters are found by getting in among the words that follow

explanation.surface: Anxiety about obstructing traffic when backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting in' finds EWA in thE WAy; 'when reversing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe is a mix of fear and reverence, dread at something mighty.

clue.text: Cold before holiday period: a nasty thing to catch

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
hol is a British informal short form of holiday
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Catching a cold just before the holidays is unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is a serious infectious disease, something unpleasant to contract.

clue.text: Hold that hurts Norman's head

parts.note: ow is what someone says when something hurts

indicators.note: the head of the name is its first letter

explanation.surface: A wrestling grip that is painful to a Norman's head.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to hold or possess it.

clue.text: Straighten out fool in humanitarian mission around South

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, undertakes humanitarian missions

indicators.note: the word for fool goes around the letter for South

parts.note: a twit is a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot on an aid mission in the south is sorted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' places S inside TWIT, before its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: To untwist a tangled thing is to straighten it.

clue.text: Not entirely against wine being consumed by soccer team? That's marvellous

indicators.note: the pieces are consumed by, swallowed inside, the team's letters

parts.note: FC, Football Club, appears in many soccer team names

indicators.note: the word for against is not used entirely, losing its last letter

parts.note: anti means against
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A football side, despite opposition, downs some wine and pronounces it superb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' drops the last letter of the word for against; 'being consumed by' puts that and the Italian wine inside the football club letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic, informally, means wonderful or excellent.

clue.text: Monarch's Queen, true — one line dying out

parts.note: R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for queen

indicators.note: the letter for one line dies out, disappearing from the pieces

parts.note: loyal means true, faithful
one L, the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: The sovereign's queen, faithful, sees a royal lineage ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dying out' removes one L from RLOYAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal is the adjective for what belongs to a monarch.
